title: Movement
description: Build responsive 2D character controllers, enemy patrols, and moving platforms using Lupis Engine's physics components and visual scripting kits.

blocks.content: Lupis Engine provides ready-to-use movement nodes in [Helper & Tool](node_library/helper_tool) along with low-level velocity and transform controls in [Physics & Collision](node_library/game_physics). Pair a [Physics Body](components/physics_body) and [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider) with a [Script Controller](components/script_controller) to move player characters, AI enemies, or environmental props.

blocks.message: Use **Platformer (Side-Scroll)** or **Top-Down** motion modes for player characters, and **Custom / Arcade** for moving platforms that should not be pushed by gravity.

rows: You want side-scrolling walking, jumping, one-way platform drop-through, and state-driven sprite animations.
You want 8-directional RPG or twin-stick movement with diagonal speed normalization, sprinting, and directional animations.
You want moving platforms, oscillating hazards, or AI enemies that patrol and chase the player.
You want to configure solid terrain, sloped ramps, triggers, and combat hitboxes.
You want to create idle, walk, run, and jump animation clips.
You want a complete step-by-step tutorial for building a playable platformer.
You want a complete step-by-step tutorial for building a top-down adventure.
